memory_update.text: Add MU as the highest-confidence US-listed direct HBM supplier for the HBM/advanced memory node.
Add TSM as the highest-confidence US-listed ADR for CoWoS/3DFabric advanced packaging capacity control.
Add AMKR as a US-listed OSAT/advanced packaging second-order candidate; evidence is strong for advanced packaging and AI targeting, but revenue specificity to HBM/AI accelerators needs further work.
Add ASML as a second-order HBM capacity enabler through advanced DRAM lithography exposure rather than direct packaging ownership.
Add ONTO as an HBM/advanced packaging process-control and metrology supplier with specific HBM manufacturer order evidence.

Non-US-listed leaders remain important for the node but are outside the US-listed focus: SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, ASE Technology, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Kinsus, Disco, Besi, ASMPT and ASM International should be tracked in a separate global coverage layer or via OTC/ADR availability checks.
MU should be retained as a direct HBM capacity candidate for the AI HBM/advanced-packaging node; official 2026 disclosure confirms HBM4 production shipments for NVIDIA Vera Rubin.
TSM should be retained as a core capacity-controller candidate because CoWoS and related advanced-packaging platforms are explicitly tied to AI demand and customer capacity planning.
ONTO and COHU are equipment-vendor candidates with direct HBM or 2.5D AI-packaging inspection/metrology evidence; they may represent less obvious chokepoint exposures than memory makers or foundries.
AMKR is a plausible second-order advanced-packaging/test capacity candidate, but later layers must distinguish broad OSAT AI/HPC exposure from true HBM or CoWoS-equivalent bottleneck control.

Not included due to the 5-candidate limit but worth checking in later passes: ASX/ASE Technology, KLAC, CAMT, FORM, ENTG, KLIC, TER, AMAT, LRCX, ASML, BESIY, Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Kinsus, Disco, and ASMPT. Some are ADR/OTC or non-US primary listings and require listing/liquidity classification.
MU is the cleanest US-listed direct HBM mapping in this node; verify HBM revenue, customer commitments, and HBM4/HBM4E ramp status in the next earnings call.
AMKR should be tracked as a US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity candidate, but the research layer must separate broad packaging exposure from true AI/HBM advanced-packaging utilization.

ONTO and CAMT are high-relevance inspection/metrology beneficiaries for HBM and advanced packaging; both have explicit HBM/AI packaging disclosures and should be compared on tool share, customer concentration, and backlog conversion.
ACMR is a less obvious advanced-packaging equipment candidate with global customer orders, but its HBM-specific linkage is an inference and needs tool-of-record/customer validation.

Non-US-listed but important node controllers remain outside this pass: SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, TSMC, ASE, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Kinsus, Disco, Besi, and ASMPT. Later layers should map US ADR/accessibility and supplier dependencies.
The expanded US-listed universe for this node clusters into: HBM capacity controller, OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity, inspection/metrology, and wafer/panel-level advanced-packaging equipment.

node: HBM, advanced memory, and advanced packaging
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for the HBM / advanced memory / advanced packaging node. Highest-confidence direct exposures in this pass are Micron as a US-listed HBM supplier, TSMC as the leading foundry and CoWoS/3DFabric capacity controller, Amkor as a US-listed outsourced advanced packaging and test provider, ASML as a lithography supplier to advanced DRAM/HBM capacity ramps, and Onto Innovation as a process-control/metrology supplier with explicit HBM manufacturer orders. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded US-listed universe for the HBM and advanced-packaging chokepoint. The strongest direct candidates are Micron for HBM supply and TSMC for CoWoS/advanced packaging capacity. Second-order but still plausible chokepoint exposures include Amkor as an OSAT packaging/test capacity provider, Onto Innovation as advanced-packaging/HBM process-control equipment, and Cohu as HBM inspection/metrology equipment. This is a research universe only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe for the AI HBM / advanced-packaging chokepoint. The strongest direct mappings are Micron as a US-listed HBM producer, Amkor as an OSAT/advanced-packaging provider, and Onto/Camtek as inspection and metrology vendors tied to HBM, micro-bumps, 2.5D/3D packaging, and heterogeneous integration. ACM Research is included as a less obvious second-order beneficiary because it has announced advanced-packaging tool orders across wafer-level and panel-level packaging; its direct HBM exposure still needs customer-level validation.
